method: The canvas sets the knot count: the rug width and length in inches are each multiplied by the mesh count in holes per inch and rounded to the nearest whole hole, because canvas is cut between holes and a partial row cannot be knotted. The default standard canvas is 3.3 holes per inch, with 4 and 5 hole fine canvas offered; a 24 in side on 3.3 mesh therefore becomes 79 holes and 23.94 in, and the page reports that trimmed size whenever rounding moved the edge. Knots are the product of the two hole counts, one knot per hole, which is the most yarn the rug can use because every hole is assumed filled. Each latch hook knot is a single strand folded through a hole and looped around the canvas thread, so the strand must span the pile twice plus an allowance for the fold: cut length = 2 x pile height + 0.5 in. That reproduces the common 2.5 in pre-cut strand for a 1 in pile on standard canvas. Total yarn is knots x cut length, increased by the waste percentage for trimming, tails and miscuts, and reported in inches, yards and metres. Skeins are the total divided by the skein yardage on the label and rounded up, because a partial skein still has to be bought; the page also reports how many strands one skein cuts and the yarn used before waste. Skein length is an input rather than a constant because a 3 oz skein is not a fixed yardage across brands. Limits are 4-240 in per side, 0.25-4 in pile, 0-50 percent waste, 1-1000 yards per skein and only the three mesh counts. The result is a purchasing estimate, not a pattern: it assumes every hole is filled and a uniform pile, and it does not model yarn thickness, dye lots, canvas thickness, the knotting style actually used, or yarn lost to joins and repairs. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Latch hook canvas is sold by mesh count in holes per inch, commonly 3.3 (standard), 4 and 5 (fine); the knot count follows the canvas, one knot per hole.
A latch hook knot is a single strand folded through a canvas hole and looped around the canvas thread, so the cut strand must cover the finished pile twice plus the fold.
Pre-cut latch hook yarn is commonly supplied in 2.5 in lengths for a 1 in pile on standard 3.3 mesh canvas, matching the 0.5 in wrap allowance used here (2 x 1 + 0.5 = 2.5 in).
Skein yardage varies by brand and weight, so the yardage printed on the skein label is an input rather than a fixed constant.
